subject: Questions about how Full-information maximum likelihood works (with lavaan)

messages.author: cfc6e44e2aaec6eb
messages.subject: Questions about how Full-information maximum likelihood works (with lavaan)
parts:
Hello, 

I am not too familiar with the SEM concepts hence I am asking my question. 

My question is about how the full-information maximum likelihood estimation works with lavaan when you specify the "missing = ML" option either with the sem or the cfa function.

I am pretty sure that the FIML method uses all available data within the dataframe and not just the variable data specifically included within the model itself. Is this correct? This means that I want to have as many original variables (even if they are not in the specified models) in the dataset or dataframe as possible rather than dropping variables that are not used in the model analysis/estimation right? 

However, when I run my SEM analysis with the full dataset (all variables collected through the surveys) and also with the reduced dataset (containing just the analysis model variables), I see no changes. What is really going on in the background when we specify "missing = ML"? How should I make sure that the FIML is using the full information in the dataset to better approximate reality (if there were no missingness)? 

Thank you very much in advance for your help!

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Questions about how Full-information maximum likelihood works (with lavaan)
parts: "Full information" means that the method models the missing values from incomplete observations while estimating model parameters. If all cases in your dataset are complete, then FIML = ML.

Hi,

 

FIML does not use variables outside the model by default. If you want to use variables outside the model, you need to specify them as auxiliary variables. For an explanation of FIML, see

 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6CQ526G8rOk&t=1s

 

And an explanation for auxiliary variables, see

 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TNLKugQg7XE

 

 

Mikko
